data.title: Card
data.tagline: Keep information about one item in a single block
data.description: A card usually groups an image, title, summary, and actions for the same object. It works well for browsing similar items. Make it clear whether the whole card is clickable; if only parts perform actions, keep links and buttons separate.

use: Group an item's image and metadata
avoid: Wrap every small piece of content in another card
Make the whole card clickable when it contains conflicting controls
Mix unrelated information in one block
Use cards when a compact list or table is easier to scan

lessonPractice.title: A template marketplace shows a grid where each item has a cover, name, author, price, and its own detail page. How should it be organized?

options.label: Give each template its own card with a clear information boundary
options.feedback: Each template is an independent browsable object, so a card can group its key information and destination.

options.label: Put every template inside one large card covering the page
options.feedback: One large container hides item boundaries and makes click targets and information ownership unclear.

options.label: Use a compact text-only data table for all templates
options.feedback: A table suits dense field comparison, but the task calls for visual browsing led by template covers.

data.agentPrompt: Make each marketplace template an independent card with cover, name, author, and price, with the main area opening its detail page. Avoid nested cards and verify inner buttons do not trigger navigation.
